meaning: A personal question you pick when you set up an account, like your first pet's name. You answer it later to prove who you are.
clues: It is something you set up to prove who you are.
You answer it with something only you should know.
It asks a question about your life, like the name of your first pet.
Answers can be guessed or found online, so experts say it should not be your only protection.
It has two words. The first has eight letters and starts with S. The second starts with Q.
assumes: A PIN is a secret number
A one-time code works only once

decoys.meaning: A short code sent to you for one sign-in only. It stops working after a few minutes.
A secret number, often four digits, that you type to prove it is you, such as to unlock a phone.
A way to open a phone by looking at it. The phone checks that your face matches the one it saved.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, the bank teller knew your face. That was our security question.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today, the answers can be easy to look up. Pick a question whose answer is not on your profile page.

sources.name: Google Online Security Blog, New Research: Some Tough Questions for Security Questions
